Grading a batch

How we sort one collection of eggs into three grades and write the batch down.

History Edit

OMLast edited by Oleh Marchenko on 14 November 2026Six minutes to read

Grading takes two people about three hours for 6 kg of eggs. Do it on the day of the last collection of a batch, in the cold room, and finish before anyone salts a single egg.

At a glance

Current batch
Batch 14, graded on 6 November
Who
Two people, one at the sieves and one at the scales
Where
The cold room, at 2 to 4 °C
Tools
Sieves of 3 and 3.5 mm, the scales, three trays
Grades
ABC

Before you start

  • The thermometer in the cold room reads between 2 and 4 °C.
  • The sieves, the trays and the spoon are washed and dry. Water left on a sieve makes the eggs stick and crack.
  • The batch book is open at a new page, with the batch number at the top.

Grade the eggs

  1. Stack the 3.5 mm sieve on the 3 mm sieve, over the C tray.
  2. Tip the eggs of one collection onto the top sieve, no more than 500 g at a time.
  3. Shake the sieves gently for 40 seconds. Longer shaking cracks the shells.
  4. Move what stays on the top sieve to the A tray, and what stays on the lower sieve to the B tray.
  5. Look over the A tray with the lamp and move any egg that is cracked, flat or grey to C.
  6. Weigh each tray without its lid and write the three weights in the batch book.

Keep the eggs below 4 °C the whole time

Eggs that sit above 4 °C for more than 20 minutes go to grade C, however good they look. If the door was left open, read the thermometer before you go on.

The three grades

The size decides the grade first, then the look. When in doubt, choose the lower grade.

Grade Size Look Goes into
A 3.5 to 4 mm Round, even, pearl white 50 g and 100 g jars
B 3 to 3.5 mm Even, a little smaller 30 g jars
C Under 3 mm Cracked, flat or grey The farm kitchen, never sold

Write the batch down

In the batch book, under the batch number, write the date, the three weights and the names of the two people who graded. Then enter the same weights in the shop under Batches, so the jars can go on sale.

Batch 14 came to 4.1 kg of A, 1.6 kg of B and 0.5 kg of C. That filled 412 jars once salted.
